description: Treat the selection of which positions to mutate as a multi-armed bandit problem. Use Thompson sampling or UCB to adaptively allocate evaluation budget to the most promising mutable positions, rapidly identifying high-value positions before optimizing amino acid choices.
mathematical_formalization: N candidate positions as arms. Reward mu_i = max_a ddG(position_i, amino_acid_a). Thompson sampling: sample theta_i ~ Beta(alpha_i, beta_i), select top-k. Evaluate, update posteriors. After T rounds, commit to top-k and optimize amino acids.
analogical_connections: Clinical trial design: allocating patients to identify best treatment
Qiu et al. (Princeton): tree search-based evolutionary bandits with Bayesian regret bounds
A/B testing: multi-armed bandit for web page optimization
implementation_hypothesis: Phase 1: Thompson sampling for 200 rounds over 50 candidate positions. Phase 2: For top-8 positions, run beam search over amino acid choices. Total: ~2000 scorer calls.
experiment_seed: Compare bandit-selected vs top-by-single-mutant-ddG vs random positions + beam search on 50 Mega-scale proteins with k={3,5,8}.
